sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Methods are like recipes in programming - they let you reuse code and keep things organized! Here's what we'll cover:

• What methods are and why they're useful
• How to create and call your own methods
• The parts that make up a method (name, parameters, return type)
• How methods help you write cleaner code

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine you're baking cookies. Instead of writing the same instructions every time you want cookies, you create a recipe card (method) that you can use again and again.

Methods work the same way in programming! They let you:

• **Package code** into reusable blocks
• **Avoid repetition** - write once, use many times
• **Organize your program** into logical pieces

Here's a simple method that says hello:
```java
void sayHello() {
    System.out.println("Hello!");
}
```

• `void` means it doesn't return anything
• `sayHello` is the method name
• The curly braces `{}` contain the code to run

sections.title: 📊 Visual Simulation
sections.content: Step-by-step visualization of how methods work:

steps.title: Writing the Method
steps.description: First, you create the method (like writing a recipe). It sits there waiting to be used.

steps.title: Calling the Method
steps.description: When you call the method, the program jumps to execute its code.

steps.title: Executing the Code
steps.description: The method runs its code, then returns to where it was called. Output appears!

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Methods are reusable blocks of code
✓ They help avoid repeating the same code
✓ Every method has a name and body (code inside {})
✓ You 'call' a method to make it run
✓ Methods can take inputs (parameters) and give back results (return values)

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Give methods clear, descriptive names (like `calculateTax` instead of `doStuff`)
Keep methods focused on doing one thing well
Test your methods separately before using them in bigger programs
donts: Don't make methods too long (aim for < 20 lines)
Don't forget the parentheses () when calling a method
Don't create methods that do too many different things
sections.protip: Start with simple methods, then gradually add parameters and return values as you get comfortable!

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Methods are everywhere in real apps! Here's how they're used:

examples.how: Use methods like `calculateInterest()`, `processTransaction()`, and `validatePassword()` to organize financial operations
Methods control character actions (`jump()`, `attack()`, `takeDamage()`) and game logic
Methods handle posting (`createPost()`), liking (`addLike()`), and notifications (`sendAlert()`)

problem.description: Create a method called `printGreeting` that takes a name as input and prints a personalized greeting. Then call it from main with your name!
hints: Your method should have one parameter of type String
Use System.out.println() to print the greeting
Remember to include the name in your greeting!
problem.explanation: The method takes a String parameter, combines it with a greeting message, and prints the result. When called with "Alex", it outputs: "Hello, Alex! Welcome to Java!"

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Methods help you organize and reuse code
📌 Every method has a name, parameters (optional), and a body
📌 Call methods by using their name followed by parentheses
📌 Practice creating simple methods before moving to more complex ones
📌 You're ready to learn about parameters and return values next!
